# The FORTRAN end-to-end programs

`docs/PHASE-75 - FORTRAN first light.md`'s subtask 8: each `name.for` is
a FORTRAN program and `name.out` what running it prints at the terminal,
followed by SHOW SYMBOL's line for `$STATUS`. `TestFortranPrograms`
(`internal/console/fortranprograms_test.go`) copies each source to a
volume, runs FORTRAN, MACRO, LINK, and RUN on govax, checks that the
first three said nothing, and compares RUN's output with `name.out`.
Every program runs with paging off; those in `fortranPagingPrograms`
run with paging on too. Every program runs compiled both ways, with `/NOOPTIMIZE`
and `/OPTIMIZE` (Phase 84), against one `name.out`; `testdata/opt84/kernels`
runs here as well.

A program that reads the terminal has a third file, `name.in`, the lines
typed at it (Phase 80, subtask 14); the test's terminal doesn't echo them,
so a reply doesn't show after its prompt.

The expected output is written from the language's rules (the *VAX
FORTRAN Language Reference Manual*, and the phase doc's choices for
list-directed output), not copied from a run: there is no VAX FORTRAN
to check against. To add a program, add both files; this directory's
`.gitignore` keeps `*.out` from the repository's own rule.

| Program | What it exercises |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| `optalias.for` | What an optimizer mustn't assume about where values are: EQUIVALENCE overlaps, COMMON changed by a call in a loop, a local changed through an address kept elsewhere, the DO variable after each way out, values kept with no SAVE, what I/O statements store, ASSOCIATEVARIABLE, dummies sharing storage to read, an unsigned character comparison (Phase 84) |
| `optasts.for` | Variables an AST routine changes, which only VOLATILE or a call can say: a routine run again by an AST, COMMON changed during a call, a loop with no call in it that only a timer's AST ends (Phase 84) |
| `optfaults.for` | Faults an optimizer mustn't move or remove: divisions by zero and a reserved operand where they never run, and divisions by zero that do run, with the result unused and the operands known (Phase 84) |
| `optbranch.for` | What the branch rules of `/OPTIMIZE` must get right: GO TO loops closing by `AOBLEQ`, `AOBLSS`, and `ACBL`, a limit that overlaps the index, loops too long for a byte branch, an arithmetic IF right after a step, chains of branches, and code nothing reaches (Phase 84) |
| `optforward.for` | What forwarding and dead code must get right: stores to part of a variable, types sharing storage, arms that agree and don't, a loop's top, DO counts of no trips, what a call changes, each settled branch, an ASSIGNed label, known character lengths, a function that keeps the last call's value, and faults that have to stay (Phase 84) |
| `optcse.for` | What common subexpressions and finding a place once must get right: each operator in place and each that can't be, each form of dummy, each thing that ends a value, a variable holding a value and one that stops, operands either way round, a short-circuited operand, VOLATILE, a format expression sharing a value with its list, and substrings (Phase 84) |
| `optinvar.for` | What moving values out of loops must get right: subscripts in nested loops; a division in a loop that doesn't run, under a test, in a test's second operand, after an exit, and after a call that never comes back; COMMON and a passed local changed in a loop, a local no call can reach, half of a variable, an element of an array being written; GO TO loops, the extended range, an assigned GO TO to a loop's top from inside and from outside, a loop that starts its routine, an ENTRY at a loop's top; a dummy that wasn't passed; adjustable arrays by a deferred index. |
| `extsource.for` | OPTIONS `/EXTEND_SOURCE`: statements to column 132 in the units that say so, a sequence field past column 72 in the one between them (Phase 85, subtask 6) |
| `optchar.for` | What making a string of one character a byte must get right: what's cut and what's filled, bytes above 127 in every comparison, known and unknown, NUL and a `TST` that can't be left out, conditions, values of two lengths, a store in a loop, overlaps with an INTEGER, COMMON, dummies, a function, a statement function, VOLATILE, a record of one byte (Phase 84) |
| `optreg.for` | What keeping values in registers must get right: every way out of a loop, what a call can see, values of every width, EQUIVALENCE, dummies of every kind, a reserved operand copied without a fault. |
| `optloop.for` | What a loop's form must keep: a DO closed on its limit, a test moved to the bottom, an index stepped in a register. |
| `rtlchars.for` | The edges of FTNRTL's character work: integer fields at a longword's limits, tabs, a record's gaps, characters past its end. Its output is FTNRTL's before Phase 84's tuning, not worked by hand. |
| `optflow.for` | Control flow that isn't a plain DO loop, and code outside a loop that reads its variables: ENTRY, assigned GO TO (one to a label its list doesn't name), the extended range, a GO TO loop, alternate returns, a variable format expression, NAMELIST, a statement function (Phase 84) |
| `aggregates.for` | Records as wholes: aggregate assignment; a record, an element, a substructure, an array, and an adjustable array of records as arguments, fields at odd offsets, a dummy record through ENTRY; %LOC and %REF; a record in COMMON with its initial values, repeated by another unit's declaration; records and array fields in unformatted I/O; array fields without subscripts as arguments, items, and an internal file; a record too long for one MOVC3 |
| `average.for` | The manual's first program (14.1) and the internals tour's: a REAL function given an array, a function reference in a PRINT list |
| `services.for` | Calling services and RTL routines as functions, with null arguments (Phase 83, subtask 5): `$GETJPIW` and `$GETSYIW` with item lists from a structure, `$BINTIM`, `$ASCTIM`, `$CRELNM`, `$TRNLNM`, `$FAO`, `$FAOL`, LIB$GETJPI, LIB$DATE_TIME, LIB$SPAWN, LIB$GET_INPUT with a prompt and at the end of its input, a service govax lacks reaching a handler that continues, and FORTRAN routines given null arguments, a function with a hidden result among them |
| `rtlcalls.for` | What the LIB$ manual's FORTRAN examples do, with its own values: ADDX, SUBX, EMUL, EDIV, POLYF, BBSSI, BBCCI, SKPC, LOCC, INDEX, and LP_LINES; a declared function CALLed; LIB$SIG_TO_RET as a handler for integer and floating division by zero; LIB$MATCH_COND on FTNRTL's error, `$UNWIND` to the establisher and to its caller, with the handler's SS$_UNWIND call; `$PUTMSG` with a FORTRAN action routine |
| `asts.for` | AST routines in FORTRAN: `$DCLAST` with a parameter, `$SETIMR` and `$QIO` completion with `$HIBER` and `$WAKE`, `$CANTIM`, `$SETAST` holding one off, I/O from an AST during a statement on another unit, an internal file, and unit 6, and AUTOMATIC and static variables in a routine an AST reenters |
| `astrace.for` | Timer ASTs among statements, every IOSTAT its own; where they land doesn't show. `TestFor83ASTEverywhere` is what covers every instruction |
| `exits.for` | Exit handlers in FORTRAN: last declared first run, the status each gets, an argument of its own, one canceled, one changing the status by `$EXIT`, units still open before FTNRTL's handler and closed after it, a unit opened by the last |
| `sysdef.for` | The definition modules built into govax: `$SSDEF`, `$JPIDEF`, `$PSLDEF`, `$FORIOSDEF`, services declared by `$SYSSRVNAM` and called as functions, a handler reading `$CHFDEF`'s `CHFDEF1` and `CHFDEF2` records, and a unit including `$SYSSRVNAM` and calling nothing |
| `sysroutines.for` | The system subroutines of appendix D (Phase 83, subtask 8): DATE into CHARACTER, BYTE and INTEGER arrays, elements, a substring, a field, short and long strings, and a passed-length dummy; TIME's forms; IDATE at both lengths; SECNDS and RAN REAL under IMPLICIT INTEGER, SECNDS adding a day once; RAN's seeds; MVBITS at both lengths, with expressions of the other length, in place, and at the limits; CALL EXIT with a status and a unit open. What depends on the time is printed as whether it agrees |
| `sysown.for` | Units of the file named DATE, SECNDS, RAN, and EXIT, which are the program's own, whatever their arguments |
| `vmstour.for` | Phase 83 end to end, in one program: the definition modules, `$GETJPIW` with an item list from a structure beside LIB$GETJPI with null arguments, STR$, a handler using `CHFDEF2` that recovers from a failed OPEN by `$UNWIND`, a timer AST re-arming itself while the program is in `$HIBER`, `$FAO`, an exit handler with `CALL EXIT`, DATE and IDATE |
| `strrtl.for` | The STR$ routines on CHARACTER variables and constants (Phase 83, subtask 9): copying, truncation's status, a position off the string, `%REF` for a character by reference, null arguments, comparisons, searches, wildcards, a signaled STR$_ILLSTRCLA made a status by LIB$SIG_TO_RET, and `$STRDEF` with `$GETMSG`'s texts |
| `recursion.for` | Recursive routines (Phase 89, subtask 4), each activation with storage of its own: a function recursing by its own name and by RESULT, mutual recursion through ENTRY, quicksort of an adjustable array, CHARACTER, REAL\*16, and COMPLEX\*16 values through hidden arguments, a local and DO loops that outlive the calls in them, permutations printed from the deepest activation, alternate returns passed back up, a statement function, a SAVE'd local and COMMON that every activation shares, ten thousand activations, and an array in each frame. gfortran prints the same, given RESULT for each direct recursion (it refuses a function's name as a call without one) and for its IEEE `-0.0` |
| `recurvfe.for` | Variable format expressions in routines active more than once (Phase 89, subtask 6), each reading its own activation's frame: a local and a dummy after the deeper activations ran, a dummy through ENTRY's cell, an adjustable array's bound, a call in an expression and an expression that recurses, a character value, a spill, a loop with R6 to R10 in use, and a statement entered again by an AST in the middle of its expressions, in a RECURSIVE unit and in one with an AUTOMATIC variable |
| `recurio.for` | Recursive routines whose I/O and arguments name their own frames (Phase 89, subtask 5), each doing its I/O after its recursive call returns: NAMELIST groups of frame variables written and read back, one of an AUTOMATIC variable in a unit that isn't recursive, an internal WRITE under way while another activation's runs, ENCODE and DECODE, an adjustable array as an item, `%DESCR` of a local, dynamic strings as an argument and an item, an OPEN's KEY= list from variables |
| `recurrtl.for` | FTNRTL under recursion (Phase 89, subtask 8): 300 internal WRITEs under way at once beneath a WRITE to unit 6, a WRITE under way on each of 50 units, RECIO_OPE at every level below a statement on the same unit, and a handler unwinding dozens of activations out of their statements: the statement its establisher's caller was in goes on, the gone statement's unit is free to a statement at its depth or above (the same frames again among them), and the gone contexts are used again, the heap not growing |
| `squares.for` | A main program with no PROGRAM statement (`SQUARES$MAIN`), DO, PRINT of a text and integers |
| `factorials.for` | INTEGER and REAL arithmetic, REAL output in G's F and E forms, mixed-mode conversions, truncating division, WRITE (\*,\*) |
| `primes.for` | Nested DO, logical IF, GO TO out of a loop, a labeled block IF, a whole array printed, a LOGICAL expression printed |
| `args.for` | SUBROUTINE, INTEGER and REAL FUNCTION, an untyped FUNCTION, arguments by reference: an actual changed, expressions copied, an array whole and from an element, RETURN in the middle, functions in expressions |
| `params.for` | PARAMETER in both forms, constants in array bounds and expressions, a CHARACTER\*(\*) constant, `**`, `//`, comparison, and intrinsic functions of constants |
| `arrays.for` | Arrays of up to seven dimensions: lower bounds of every sign, bounds from constants and REAL expressions, column-major order seen through whole-array output and one-dimensional dummies, assumed-size dummies with lower bounds, an array passed from an element, a REAL subscript |
| `common.for` | COMMON, blank and named, under other names in other units; a block lengthened by EQUIVALENCE and seen whole from another unit; a REAL's bits read through an INTEGER; arrays overlaid in `$LOCAL` |
| `data.for` | DATA and initial values in type statements, in `$LOCAL` and in COMMON from a BLOCK DATA named in EXTERNAL; a value kept by SAVE from call to call; section 4.3's byte rules read through EQUIVALENCE (numbers converted, octal, hexadecimal, Hollerith, and character constants, codes for CHARACTER\*1 items); implied-DO lists over two dimensions, with steps |
| `overlay.for` | EQUIVALENCE overlays: a matrix filled through a vector, a multidimensional array's element by its number, two lists chained into one group, a LOGICAL's and a REAL's bits read and changed through an INTEGER, an overlay's neighbors left alone, a common block under an overlay in two units |
| `parts.for` | Phase 88's indexed files: an inventory by part number (an ascending integer), by name (a character key with duplicates), and by quantity (a descending integer), every specifier on each, READ in sequence after a keyed one, REWRITE moving a record in its keys' orders, DELETE, a number used again, each failure's IOSTAT, OPENs with fewer keys, none, and the wrong ones; and formatted records on a descending character key |
| `shared.for` | Two units sharing an indexed file: a record one holds is SPERECLOC to the other until UNLOCK or its next READ, each unit its own key and place, what one writes or deletes seen by the other at once, a READONLY unit, and a file opened without SHARED |
| `tables.for` | Tables set by DATA and put to use: days in the months, a binary search, an interpolation, tax brackets in a common block from a BLOCK DATA, a matrix product of matrices given by rows and by columns |
| `store.for` | The internals tour's program for storage (section 8): PARAMETER in a bound, COMMON from a BLOCK DATA, EQUIVALENCE, DATA and initial values |
| `lengths.for` | INTEGER and LOGICAL of every length: unsigned constants in short variables, word arithmetic wrapping, a small constant beside a word, mixed lengths, the logical operators bit by bit, conversions, short conditions, a word DO variable and function, short arguments with subscripts, OPTIONS /NOI4 for one unit |
| `reals.for` | REAL\*8 in D_floating and REAL\*16: a REAL\*8 constant's digits and a REAL\*4's widened, rounding back to REAL\*4, mixed types, G editing's two forms at each width, a REAL\*8 DO variable, truncation to an integer, a REAL\*8 function, a REAL\*8 array changed by a subroutine, expressions that spill |
| `realsg.for` | `reals.for` in G_floating, each unit's OPTIONS /G_FLOATING saying so: 15 digits and three-digit exponents, and a value past D_floating's range |
| `complex.for` | COMPLEX\*8 and COMPLEX\*16 in D_floating: constants and their output, sums, differences, negation, mixed with REAL and INTEGER, products in line and by OTS$MULCD_R3, quotients by OTS$DIVC and OTS$DIVCD_R3, conversion to the real part, .EQ. and .NE., arrays with subscripts that aren't constant, a COMPLEX function, a COMPLEX argument changed by a subroutine, COMPLEX\*8 with REAL\*8, a record too full for the next value |
| `complexg.for` | `complex.for` in G_floating, each unit's OPTIONS /G_FLOATING saying so, and a product past D_floating's range |
| `chars.for` | CHARACTER values: assignment filling with blanks and cutting, substrings with constant bounds and with bounds that aren't (as values, targets, and output items), overlapping moves, a whole array and its elements' substrings, comparisons as values and as conditions with the shorter padded, ASCII's order past 127, a CHARACTER's bytes through EQUIVALENCE, a common block another unit changes |
| `strings.for` | CHARACTER arguments and concatenation: variables, constants, substrings, elements, and expressions passed by descriptor; passed-length dummies and one of a declared length; a dummy changed, and a parenthesized argument's copy; arrays passed whole, from an element, passed on, and seen with shorter elements; concatenations in a temporary, one overlapping its target, and ones of a passed-length dummy in a dynamic string, as values, arguments, output items, and conditions |
| `powers.for` | `**` on every type: INTEGER, REAL, and REAL\*8 and REAL\*16 powers to constant exponents from 1 to 8 in line, in the `OTS$` routines' order; larger, negative, and zero exponents and ones that aren't constant by `OTS$POWJJ`, `POWII`, `POWRJ`, `POWDJ`, `POWHJ_R3`; REAL exponents by `POWRR`, `POWDD`, `POWHH_R3`, and a REAL\*4 with a REAL\*8 by `POWRD` and `POWDR`; an INTEGER\*2 power wrapping in a word; a base computed once, `-X**2`, powers in subscripts and a condition; COMPLEX powers always by `POWCJ`, `POWCC`, `POWCDJ_R3`, `POWCDCD_R3`; and a unit under OPTIONS /G_FLOATING with `POWGJ`, `POWGG` (a REAL\*4 with a REAL\*8 too), `POWCGJ_R3`, `POWCGCG_R3` |
| `intrinsics.for` | The intrinsic functions written in line: ABS, MAX, MIN, DIM, SIGN, and MOD of INTEGERs, REALs, and words, generic and specific; INT, NINT, IFIX, ZEXT, REAL, DBLE, and footnote 10's default integer (a unit under OPTIONS /NOI4); COMPLEX parts, CMPLX, DCMPLX, CONJG, DPROD; IAND, IOR, IEOR, NOT, ISHFT, IBITS, IBSET, IBCLR, BTEST on words and longwords, and ISHFTC by FTNRTL's `FTN$IISHFTC` and `FTN$JISHFTC`; LEN, INDEX, ICHAR, CHAR, and the lexical comparisons, of passed-length dummies too; the choosing functions in a condition, a DO loop's limit, a subscript, and a statement with a dynamic string |
| `jumps.for` | The jumps of sections 5.6 and 5.7.1: the computed GO TO in range and out of it, with INTEGER, INTEGER\*2, and REAL indexes; ASSIGN and the assigned GO TO with a list and without, in the main program and through a dummy argument; the arithmetic IF of INTEGER, INTEGER\*2, REAL, and REAL\*8 values, with three labels and with two the same |
| `stops.for` | STOP from a subroutine, its display of digits kept as written; RETURN and END in a subroutine and in a function, whose value is the one last assigned to its name |
| `stopdo.for` | STOP as a DO loop's terminal statement, which ends the program on the first pass |
| `loops.for` | The loops of sections 5.3 and 5.4: DO without a label, ended by END DO, with positive, negative, and REAL steps, nested, and run no times; DO WHILE ended by END DO, by a labeled terminal statement, and by a labeled END DO, and run no times; a jump to a labeled END DO for the next pass; a DO and a DO WHILE sharing a terminal statement; a jump out of a loop, and the extended range, out and back in every pass |
| `adjust.for` | The arrays of sections 6.1.1.1 to 6.1.1.3: the manual's SUM and X(-I/2:I/2,J), whose bounds stay what they were on entry; one array seen in several shapes, bounds in a common block and a list of expressions, lower bounds of every sign, an adjustable array with an assumed size; ENTRY points that define an array and one that doesn't, falling into an ENTRY statement; REAL\*8, COMPLEX, COMPLEX\*16, and INTEGER\*2 elements; CHARACTER arrays of a declared length, of a passed length, and passed-length with an assumed size; a whole array written and passed on, an element as the array's start, SIZEOF, and an array with no elements |
| `grades.for` | Block IF with ELSE IF and ELSE, a nested block IF, GO TO from a block to the loop's end, LOGICAL output, STOP with a display |
| `mathfns.for` | The intrinsic functions MTHRTL computes, called with their arguments by reference: square roots, exponentials, logarithms, the trigonometric functions in radians and degrees, and the hyperbolic ones in F, D, and H; AINT, ANINT, and MOD of REALs; the complex functions, F values in R0 and R1 and D values through a hidden argument, as REAL\*16 values come back too; ISHFT by a count that isn't constant (`MTH$JISHFT`, `MTH$IISHFT`); a function of a function, in a subscript, and in a condition. Its output was worked out to 80 digits apart from govax, each value rounded to its format's bits |
| `mathfnsg.for` | `mathfns.for`'s REAL\*8 and COMPLEX\*16 functions in G_floating, the unit's OPTIONS statement saying so (`MTH$GSQRT`, `MTH$CGSQRT`, ...), and values past D_floating's range |
| `mixed.for` | Mixed arithmetic end to end (Phase 78, subtask 10): a value carried through every type and back by Table 3-1 (a byte keeping an INTEGER\*2's low bits); operations between types of every rank, LOGICAL values as integers, COMPLEX\*8 with REAL\*8 and COMPLEX\*16 with REAL\*16; a REAL\*4 constant keeping its digits in a REAL\*8 expression where a REAL\*4 variable doesn't; REAL subscripts and DO limits, an INTEGER\*2 and a REAL\*8 array summed by a subroutine; mixed types in conditions; one polynomial by Horner's rule in REAL\*8, REAL\*16, and COMPLEX |
| `mixedg.for` | `mixed.for` in G_floating, each unit's OPTIONS statement saying so |
| `text.for` | Character handling end to end: a line split into words by INDEX, sorted by LLT, a word reversed in place, palindromes, lowercase and a Caesar cipher through ICHAR, CHAR, and MOD, the letters counted, a number written as its digits, a title centered by LEN, a sentence built of substrings and cut to its target's length |
| `numeric.for` | Numerical methods end to end, each result checked against a tolerance or rounded where its last digits depend on the rounding along the way: Newton's method beside SQRT, a quadratic's real and complex roots by CSQRT, Simpson's rule over SIN, pi from ATAN in F, D, and H, degrees, logarithms, a hyperbolic identity, a mean and standard deviation, compound interest, a linear system by elimination, Euclid's algorithm |

## Programs of several files

Each directory of `modules/` is one program, run by `TestFortranModules`
in both paging modes. Its `.for` files are compiled and assembled
separately, and any other file but the two below (an INCLUDE file) is
only copied to the volume. `links.txt` has one LINK command's modules per
line: the program is linked each way, and must print `name.out`, named
for the directory, every time.

| Program | What it exercises |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| `modules/aligned` | `/ALIGN` across two files, linked in both orders: LINK keeps the larger of the block's two alignments |
| `modules/psects` | CDEC$ PSECT's attributes across two files, linked in both orders: a page-aligned block, an LCL block that is still one section in the image's one cluster, a NOWRT block with its values from a BLOCK DATA |
| `modules/store` | The manual's example of a program of several files (14.1): one block seen from two files, its values from a BLOCK DATA in a third |
| `modules/procs` | Procedures passed between files: a function and its entry point, a subroutine in the calling file, a CHARACTER function of the length the caller declares, and `%VAL(%LOC(ANOTE))`, linked in both orders |
| `modules/altreturns` | Alternate returns across files, from a subroutine and its entry point, linked in both orders |
| `modules/ledger` | Four files sharing common blocks, blank and named: one block's layout from an INCLUDE file, another's declared at three lengths and in another file lengthened by EQUIVALENCE, its values from a BLOCK DATA in a file of its own that EXTERNAL names; the modules linked in three orders, so that the main program's short declaration, the module with the values, or another view of the block comes first |
| `flow.for` | Chapters 5 and 6 together: an RPN calculator (a stack of entry points, errors by alternate return, a computed GO TO on each character's class), Simpson's rule through a dummy procedure, bisection with a function passed on and called from a statement function, a matrix product on adjustable arrays, an assigned GO TO in a loop, and the manual's hyperbolic functions |
| `callback.for` | A FORTRAN routine as VMS sees it: a LIB$ESTABLISH condition handler, a SYS$DCLAST AST routine, and what LIB$CALLG calls |
| `handlers.for` | Condition handlers: which of FTNRTL's errors a handler can go on from, `$CHFDEF`'s structures, `$UNWIND`, LIB$SIG_TO_RET, LIB$MATCH_COND, LIB$FIXUP_FLT, LIB$INT_OVER, LIB$FLT_UNDER, and continuing a LIB$STOP |
| `stmtfuncs.for` | Statement functions: the manual's VOLUME, SINH, AVG, and CSF; dummy arguments named for other entities; every type of value; those using earlier ones, and one in another's argument; constants, variables, elements, expressions, and CHARACTER values of other lengths as actual arguments; the value converted to the function's type and length, and copied when passed; in conditions and DO's parameters |
| `procs.for` | Procedures as arguments: functions of every kind of value, subroutines, entry points, and intrinsics through dummy procedures, passed on, reached through ENTRY's cells, with alternate returns; CHARACTER functions and the length that goes with them (`CHARACTER*(*)` dummies in dynamic strings); null arguments seen by `%LOC`; Hollerith and character constants for numbers, the manual's example where the routine is itself a dummy; `%VAL` (sign extension, `ZEXT`, REAL\*4's bits, `%VAL(%LOC(X))`), `%REF`, and `%DESCR` of each kind of argument, each read back by a FORTRAN routine |
| `funcs.for` | Functions whose values go through a hidden first argument: CHARACTER of a fixed length, the default length, a length after the name, and passed-length (the manual's REPEAT, at two lengths in two units), in every kind of expression and with the name passed on; REAL\*16 and COMPLEX\*16 typed every way; `H = F(H)` where the function writes its name before reading its argument |
| `altreturns.for` | Alternate returns: the manual's CHECK, whose arguments after the `*`s still reach it; RETURN i below and past the range, of a REAL, and of an expression; `*` and `&`; a specifier in a logical IF's CALL, in a CALL ending a DO loop, and several to one label; a return passed on through two subroutines; entry points with their `*`s in other places; a concatenation's dynamic string freed before the jump; RETURN i in a routine with no `*`s |
| `entries.for` | ENTRY statements: a subroutine's dummies in two orders, a dummy only an ENTRY names, control falling past an ENTRY, an ENTRY before the declarations, an assumed-size array and a passed length through their cells; the manual's hyperbolic functions, a function returning a different type by each entry point, names sharing a value, and CHARACTER, passed-length, and REAL\*16 and COMPLEX\*16 functions with hidden arguments |
| `funcsg.for` | `funcs.for`'s COMPLEX\*16 functions in G_floating, each unit's OPTIONS /G_FLOATING saying so, a value past D_floating's range |
| `vfe.for` | Variable format expressions (Phase 80, subtask 8): the manual's example, every kind of number, when each is computed, a function doing I/O, dummy arguments reached through the routine's AP, ENTRY's cells, ASSIGN, the ranges (VFEVALERR), and SYNERRFOR in a run-time format |
| `internal.for` | Internal files, ENCODE, and DECODE: READ and WRITE on a string beside the old forms, appendix A.1's examples, numeric buffers, an array, an element, a computed substring, dummies, END=, ERR=, a 300-byte record, and a file used during a unit's statement |
| `runformat.for` | Run-time formats (section 8.7): the manual's example, numeric and character arrays and elements, a concatenation, a substring, a function's value, a dummy, a variable changed between uses, and one found wrong when used |
| `formats.for` | Formatted output through FTNRTL's format interpreter (Phase 80, subtask 4): text and H constants, X, T, TL, and TR, slashes, a group with a colon, reversion to a group, a `$` record continued by a `+` one, run-time formats in a variable and an array, A of several widths and of an integer, Q passing an item over, TYPE, and the conditions SYNERRFOR, INFFORLOO (taken by ERR=), and OUTSTAOVE past column 133 |
| `intedit.for` | Integer and logical editing (Phase 80, subtask 5): I with minimum digits, SP and SS, and I3.0 of 0; O and Z of an integer, a word, and a byte; L; the default widths of Table 8-4; Z and O of a REAL's bytes; asterisks and OUTCONERR, the statement going on; I of a REAL, FORVARMIS at the statement's end, its record written |
| `floatedit.for` | Floating editing (Phase 80, subtask 6): F, E, D, and G with widths and digits; the scale factor and how long it lasts; SP and SS; complex values as two fields; the default widths of Table 8-4 by the item's type; the forms G chooses; asterisks and OUTCONERR, the statement going on; F of an INTEGER, FORVARMIS at the statement's end, its records written |
| `inventory.for` | Formatted input end to end (Phase 80, subtask 14), `inventory.in` its records: fixed columns read by a FORMAT until END=, a bad number taken by ERR= and counted, a price with no decimal point placed by F8.2, a short record padded with blanks; a report with headings at tab stops, repeated characters, a line per item, totals, a title written to an internal file, and the totals as a NAMELIST group |
| `dialog.for` | An interactive program (Phase 80, subtask 14), `dialog.in` what is typed: prompts left open by `$`, a command loop ended by the input's end, ACCEPT with A and list-directed (a repeat count, a null value, a slash), a bad number taken by IOSTAT=, a NAMELIST group read from the terminal and written back |
| `positions.for` | REWIND, BACKSPACE, and ENDFILE (Phase 81, subtask 6): back and forth over records, BACKSPACE at the start and after the end of the file, a write after a read ending the file, ENDFILE's records read past, each statement on a direct, fixed, and invalid unit with its FOR number, a unit ENDFILE connects with no form yet, APPEND's BACKSPACE before and after a REWIND, ENDFILE on a READONLY unit |
| `direct.for` | Direct access READ and WRITE, FIND, DEFINE FILE, and ASSOCIATEVARIABLE (Phase 81, subtask 8): records written out of order and read back, the records between them zeros, a REAL record number, the associated variable walking a file, a record past the end (ATTACCNON), one too long (OUTSTAOVE, written as far as it goes), record 0 (RECNUMOUT), a sequential READ of a direct unit (MIXFILACC), FIND and NEXTREC, a format of two records writing two, a unit DEFINE FILE describes opened by its first WRITE and, described again, by a READ, and MAXREC's limit |
| `unformatted.for` | Unformatted sequential READ and WRITE (Phase 81, subtask 7): a record of every type read back, whole arrays and implied-DO lists, a READ taking less than its record or asking for more (INPSTAREQ), one with no list passing a record over, END=; a record of two segments read and BACKSPACEd over; a unit with no OPEN connected unformatted and segmented, and ENDFILE's record read; VARIABLE records too long (OUTSTAOVE), FIXED ones filled out, read as SEGMENTED (SEGRECFOR); each form's statements on the other's units (MIXFILACC) |
| `align.for` | `/ALIGN`'s groups (Phase 82, subtask 8): natural structures, an octaword COMPLEX, a union moved to its boundary, a packed substructure, a record array's stride, COMMONS=NATURAL and STANDARD in nested groups, initial values, `$LOCAL`'s boundary across a module's routines |
| `itemlist.for` | A `$GETJPIW` item list from a structure (Phase 82, subtask 9), its bytes and addresses read back through a union's other maps, under `/WARN=ALIGNMENT`, which says nothing |
| `records.for` | Records and scalar field references (Phase 82, subtask 3): structures' initial values, a union's two maps, an array of records and an array field by subscripts that aren't constant (packed, so through computed addresses), a substructure, substrings of a field, fields as arguments, COMPLEX fields, a field as an internal file, IOSTAT=, a DO limit, and in a statement function |
| `directives.for` | The CDEC$ directives (Phase 82, subtask 7): IDENT, TITLE, and SUBTITLE before, in, and after units, in a loop and a union; PSECT's ALIGN= seen in where one-byte blocks land between aligned ones, blank common, a directive before its block's COMMON or its unit, a default written out in one unit only; a NOWRT block given values by a BLOCK DATA, read, then stored to: the ACCVIO, at the address the program prints |
| `automatic.for` | AUTOMATIC, STATIC, and VOLATILE (Phase 82, subtask 6): variables in the frame in every kind of reference (scalars, arrays, CHARACTER values and substrings, records and fields, COMPLEX, a DO variable, a statement function, arguments, whole arrays in I/O lists, an internal file, ASSIGN), each entry point's frame, a call's own values when a function calls itself through its argument against STATIC's shared one, variable format expressions, an EQUIVALENCE group, a frame of many pages; a VOLATILE block and name |
| `typeless.for` | Constants with no type of their own (Phase 82, subtask 5): octal, hexadecimal, and Hollerith constants beside an operator, assigned (bits that are no number moved, not faulting, in every floating width), with nothing to take a type from, as subscripts, DO limits, and substring bounds; character constants in numeric contexts; arguments; a statement function's value; RADIX-50 in DATA and initial values, short, long, repeated, and in lowercase; the default integer under `/NOI4` |
